:::{#def-affine-map}
#### Affine transformation

An **affine transformation** is a function $f: \mathbb{R}^p \to \mathbb{R}^m$
composed of a linear map followed by a translation
(a [composition](sets-functions.qmd#def-composition), with the linear map as the inner function):

$$f(\vx) = \matr{A} \vx + \vec{b}, \qquad \matr{A} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times p}, \quad \vec{b} \in \mathbb{R}^m$$

For a scalar-valued function ($m = 1$), this is an inner product plus an offset:

$$f(\vx) = \vec{w}^\top \vx + b, \qquad \vec{w} \in \mathbb{R}^p, \quad b \in \mathbb{R}$$ {#eq-linear-scalar}

When $\vec{b} \neq \vzero$ (or $b \neq 0$), an affine transformation does not send $\vzero$ to $\vzero$,
so it is not strictly linear.
In machine learning and statistics, functions of this form are commonly referred to as
**linear models** or linear functions, with $\vec{b}$ (or $b$) called the **bias** or **intercept**.
:::
